'''Robert C. Elston''' (born 4 February 1932) is a British born [[statistical genetics|statistical geneticist]] and distinguished professor emeritus at [[Case Western Reserve University]]. He is one of the eponyms of the [[Elston–Stewart algorithm]] and [[Haseman–Elston regression]].

==Life==
Elston was born in [[London, England]] in 1932.

In the 1970s he worked with John Stewart to create the [[Elston–Stewart algorithm]] which enables researchers to estimate the likelihood of genotype data given a [[pedigree chart|pedigree]].<ref>Elston, R. C., Stewart, J. (1970) "A new test of association for continuous variables", Biometrics, 26, 305–314</ref>

In 1980s Elston was working at [https://www.medschool.lsuhsc.edu/ the Louisiana State University Medical School] in [[New Orleans]] working on statistical genetics. Elston left LSU for Case Western Reserve University in Cleveland in 1995 taking other staff with him.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=https://nihsearch.cit.nih.gov/catalyst/2006/06.03.01/page2.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170201034353/https://nihsearch.cit.nih.gov/catalyst/2006/06.03.01/page2.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=February 1, 2017|title=Marriage of the Minds: Co-Equals Chair Inherited Disease Research Branch|last=Ross|first=Karen|date=March 2006|website=NIH Catalyst|access-date=2019-07-03}}</ref>
